trajectory_summary: The call opens cooperatively and the rep runs verify cleanly, holding setter scope well against two separate pricing-ballpark pushes. But from minute 11 onward the customer reveals he is comparing four vendors, ranks Ion last, and prefers a competitor's drone/satellite process -- and the rep never probes this intel or locks a hard appointment time, ending on a customer-controlled callback promise.
outcome_dispute: This should be read as a callback, not a booked or tentative appointment -- Kurt explicitly says he will call Ion back to set a time once he sends the bill, and no day/time was agreed on this call.

observed_outcome.quote: K. I'll give you guys a callback to set a a time since you want me here first time.
observed_outcome.reasoning: No day or time was agreed. Kurt explicitly says he will call Ion back once he sends over the bill and coordinates timing, meaning the next step is owned by the customer, not the rep -- this is a callback, not a booked or tentative appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: I could be all the way up to during the summer, probably about $2.80.
bill_anchor_audit.flip_quote: Well, yeah, that's definitely pretty hefty bill. All the rates went up. Yeah. All the rates went up everywhere.... So, yeah, solar definitely makes sense, especially, nowadays and, you know, with everything going on in the world.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep attempted a flip -- moving from bill acknowledgment to asserting solar relevance -- but it was generic (rates rising everywhere, world events) rather than anchored to Kurt's specific $280 summer / $190 winter figures. This is a diluted attempt, not a clean strategic flip, and not a full omission either; the coaching note is to sharpen the flip by reusing the customer's own number.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: Just different things that are going on in the world.... deals out there. Energy cost. The V and A, all that stuff.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: Kurt gives a diffuse reason (general world events, energy costs, VA-related info) but the rep never circles back to it explicitly when pitching the program or setting the appointment -- the later bill-flip attempt at 04:36 gestures at 'everything going on in the world' but does not tie it back to Kurt's stated reason as a deliberate reinforcement.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: I pretty much like the, the way the other company handled it.
primary_coaching_focus.why: Across three separate disclosures (05:22, 11:25, 12:52) Kurt hands the rep concrete competitive information -- vendor names implied, a preferred imaging process, and an explicit ranking putting Ion third or fourth -- and the rep never asks a single follow-up question. This is the single highest-value, lowest-cost fix on this call and directly affects what the closer walks into blind.
